papers.title: Decoupled Predictive Decision Making: A Shared Conditional Predictor for Agents

summary.tldr: Decoupled Predictive Decision Making (DPDM) improves agent decisions by combining a frozen language model semantic encoder with a shared, frozen conditional predictor (LimiX-2) that infers task targets from deployment evidence without parameter updates.
key_points: DPDM uses a two-part architecture: language models (such as Qwen3.5-27B) generate semantic representations of evidence, while a single frozen LimiX-2 conditional predictor maps evidence and queries to choices using a unified interface.
The system operates entirely via in-context empirical inference using deployment evidence, requiring zero neural parameter updates for either the semantic encoder or the conditional predictor.

Evaluated across 50 benchmarks, DPDM with Qwen3.5-27B raised mean accuracy from 78.80% (few-shot prompting) to 84.92% at evaluated history budgets, and reached 82.33% when using identical histories and queries.
On ToolPRMBench, DPDM achieved absolute accuracy gains of 34.26% on BFCL tasks and 28.87% on ToolSandbox tasks at respective history budgets.
Across five reasoning-step assessment tasks and four encoders, DPDM increased mean balanced accuracy by an absolute 14.51% under identical imbalanced histories.
summary.why_it_matters: By decoupling semantic representation from empirical inference, DPDM allows LLM agents to continuously learn from deployment history and improve decision accuracy without costly model fine-tuning.

papers.title: VFlash: Fast, Accurate Visual Planning via Flash Primitive Decoding

summary.tldr: VFlash introduces Flash Primitive Decoding, a method using a lightweight drafter to predict structured visual primitives jointly in a single forward pass instead of token-by-token.
key_points: Replaces autoregressive coordinate-by-coordinate decoding with a lightweight drafter that generates an entire visual primitive (boxes, points, trajectories) in one forward pass.
Adapts its prediction layout dynamically based on the primitive's type, dimensionality, and variable length.
Trains directly on annotated primitives and accepts valid structural predictions without requiring exact target-token agreement with the autoregressive model.
Achieves ~25x faster generation for 3D point motion forecasting and improves spatial accuracy over standard autoregressive decoding.
Boosts average success rates of a conditioned world action model from 62.6% to 70.2% across four MolmoSpaces task suites.
summary.why_it_matters: By drastically reducing generation latency while improving spatial accuracy, VFlash enables real-time visual goal and trajectory planning for physical AI systems like robotics and autonomous driving.

papers.title: Harness-S: Learning from Sibling Harnesses for Generalizable Agent Training

summary.tldr: Harness-S uses a fixed pool of specialized sibling harnesses to rescue failed policy attempts during training, distilling auxiliary execution capabilities into a single policy that executes under the original base harness.
key_points: Directional Harness Evolution creates a fixed Sibling Harness Pool of specialized variants designed to repair different failure modes.

Complementary Harness Rescue Training activates auxiliary harnesses only after initial attempts under the base harness fail, using the resulting successful trajectories for policy reinforcement learning.
An Adaptive Harness Router selects the top-k harness variants using LLM voting and Harness Behavior Profiles, which are continuously re-anchored as the policy evolves.
The method demonstrates performance gains across AppWorld, SWE-Gym, and DBBench when evaluated on the original base harness, with optional Rank-1 router reuse during inference.
summary.why_it_matters: It allows AI agents to internalize capabilities discovered through diverse, specialized execution environments without requiring complex or non-standard harnesses at deployment time.

papers.title: Random Is Almost Enough? Stable and Low-Cost Benchmark Compression via BestRand

summary.tldr: BestRand is a benchmark compression method that mitigates random sampling's high-error tail while cutting subset construction costs and improving out-of-distribution estimation accuracy.
key_points: Analytical approximation of subset estimation errors reveals a long-tailed distribution where instability persists even as model counts increase.
BestRand reduces high-error risk by 50.2% and average estimation error by 16.4% compared to existing competitive compression methods.
The method uses 51.3% of the construction cost of baseline methods and lowers out-of-distribution estimation error by 21.8% across temporal, model-family, and score-range shifts.
Extensively validated on over 70 text, multimodal, agent, and Vision-Language-Action (VLA) benchmarks.
summary.why_it_matters: It enables stable, accurate, and cheap LLM and multimodal evaluation by preventing the rare, massive estimation errors inherent to basic random sampling.

papers.title: WeLM-Image: A Unified Image Generation Model towards Visual Intelligence

summary.tldr: WeLM-Image is a unified image foundation model using a Mixture-of-Transformers architecture with sparse Mixture-of-Experts to integrate multimodal understanding into text-to-image generation, editing, and multi-reference synthesis.
key_points: Uses a Mixture-of-Transformers (MoT) backbone combining shared attention with split parameter paths for understanding and generation to prevent optimization interference.
Incorporates MoE modules routing to 31.7B total parameters while activating ~5.4B generation parameters per target latent token.
Employs a data engine with a knowledge-grounded visual vocabulary and visual clustering, training up to native 1.5K (1536 resolution) using bilingual annotations.
Consolidates specialized generation and editing policies trained via rubric/checklist rewards using noise-aware on-policy distillation.
WeLM-Image-Turbo achieves single-GPU execution via MeanFlow few-step distillation, generating a 1024x1024 image in 4.98 seconds on an NVIDIA H20 using 8 guidance-free steps.
summary.why_it_matters: It enables high-resolution image generation, instruction editing, and multi-reference synthesis within a single unified model efficient enough for single-GPU consumer deployments.

papers.title: TailSteer: Trajectory-Tail Steering for Drift-Resistant Multi-turn Image Editing

summary.tldr: TailSteer is a final-stage training framework that prevents multi-turn visual drift by concentrating preservation corrections at the tail of on-policy denoising trajectories.
key_points: Targets long-term visual drift in multi-turn image editing where small unintended changes accumulate across repeated output reuses.
Keeps early denoising dynamics close to the base model while applying learned preservation corrections near the trajectory tail to suppress fine-grained deviations.
Trains on the editor's own on-policy denoising rollouts using unchanged source content as a reference, eliminating the need for curated ground-truth editing pairs.
Demonstrates substantial reduction in cumulative drift across 15-20 editing turns on FLUX, SenseNova, and Qwen model families without degrading single-turn editing or text-to-image benchmarks.
summary.why_it_matters: It allows foundation image models to sustain robust multi-turn editing over long horizons without requiring expensive retraining or specialized inference-time mechanisms.

papers.title: SLA: Scaling Spatial-Language-Action Model via Continual Pre-training

summary.tldr: SLA is a Spatial-Language-Action model that integrates implicit spatial alignment into continual pre-training for VLAs using 3D perception supervision without adding inference overhead.
key_points: Initialized from a pretrained pi05 policy, SLA jointly optimizes action prediction and spatial alignment between intermediate visual embeddings and a frozen 3D perception model.
Employs feature-dependent gates to adaptively aggregate multi-layer visual embeddings for spatial supervision across diverse embodiments and scenes.
Utilizes a teacher model leveraging partial depth, camera calibration, and RGB data to handle heterogeneous geometric annotations.
Applies probabilistic state dropout during training to prevent trajectory overfitting and promote reliance on visual cues.
Discard all auxiliary training components at inference time, retaining the original VLA architecture and weights.
summary.why_it_matters: It establishes transferable 3D spatial understanding as a foundational capability in vision-language-action models while maintaining zero additional computational cost during deployment.

papers.title: EvoMemState: Evolving Memory State for Personal Agents

summary.tldr: EvoMemState is a state-centric long-term memory framework for LLM agents that augments persistent facts with evolving Relational States and a request-specific Reasoning State trained via reinforcement learning.
key_points: Replaces fact-centric paradigms by introducing Relational States to track fact validity, scope, and evolving relations as new facts emerge.
Utilizes Ontology-Guided Memory State Induction to extract Persistent Facts and construct their corresponding Relational States.
Employs RL-Based State Evolution to train a policy via reinforcement learning that generates a Reasoning State tailored to the current request.
Implements State-Aware Reasoning to combine facts, Relational States, and Reasoning States to direct agent responses.
summary.why_it_matters: It improves retrieval completeness and response accuracy in long-term personal AI agents by explicitly modeling how facts conflict, relate, and apply to specific user requests over time.

papers.title: D3D: Decoupled Diffusion Drafting for Asynchronous Speculative Decoding

summary.tldr: D3D is a standalone diffusion drafter that decouples candidate generation from target-model hidden states, enabling asynchronous speculative decoding by drafting successor blocks concurrently during target verification.
key_points: Combines blockwise denoising with auxiliary autoregressive supervision to generate long accepted token prefixes independently of target hidden states.
Enables drafting successor blocks during verification in a single packed pass for asynchronous execution.
Employs layer pruning based on acceptance length impact, where removing 5 of 36 layers retains over 99% of mean acceptance length on Qwen3-8B.
Achieves average speedups of 5.00x on Qwen3-8B and 5.71x on Qwen3-32B across seven benchmarks, outperforming DFlash (4.03x and 3.67x) and reaching 7.48x on GSM8K.
summary.why_it_matters: By eliminating sequential dependencies between drafting and target verification, D3D significantly increases inference throughput for large language models without degrading acceptance performance.

papers.title: Towards Foundation Decision Models: Drex

summary.tldr: Drex is a family of four open decision models (up to 27B parameters) that output probability distributions over user-provided options in a single forward pass without autoregressive decoding.
key_points: Model family includes four open architectures: 8B (DLM), 9B (v1.5), 35B with 3B active (v2.0), and 27B (Max).
Training uses supervised fine-tuning combined with reinforcement learning from adjusted feedback (RLAF), consistency losses for option-order robustness, and vision tuning for Max.
Drex Max achieves a 67.52 score on Decision Index 0.4.1 (outperforming Jev 1.14.0 at 60.70) and top decision model accuracy on DecideBench.
Drex Max processes requests in 183 ms, compared to ~2.0 s for GPT-6 Sol and ~3.5 s for Claude Opus 5.5, while maintaining output stability under option reordering.
summary.why_it_matters: Decision models like Drex dramatically reduce latency and inference costs while providing consistent, non-autoregressive output formats for structured classification and scoring tasks.

papers.title: VisSearch-Bench: Evaluating Long Horizon Visual Search in Multimodal Agents

summary.tldr: VisSearch-Bench introduces 204 human-written tasks across 5 search categories to evaluate multimodal agents on long-horizon visual search and visual context management.
key_points: Benchmark contains 204 human-written tasks covering 7 main domains, 25 subdomains, and 5 search categories including Set-wise, Sequential, Hybrid Wide-Deep, Competitive Disambiguation, and Visual-Structure-Guided Search.
Evaluation uses Accuracy for total task success and Process Score to measure the completeness and correctness of subquestion answers and intermediate results.
Evaluated across 16 multimodal models, the top-performing system achieved a full task solution rate of only 26.47% despite having access to search tools.
summary.why_it_matters: Current multimodal models struggle significantly with tasks requiring long-horizon reasoning that bridges visual evidence, spatial relations, and web search retrieval.

papers.title: Hybrid Computer Use: A Unified Programmatic, Semantic, and Visual Interface for General Agents

summary.tldr: Hybrid Computer Use (HCU) is a unified interface for general agents that combines programmatic, accessibility-based semantic, and visual GUI interactions to improve execution efficiency and accuracy.
key_points: HCU integrates three interaction channels: programmatic (code and CLI), semantic (accessibility/AX trees), and visual (GUI).
AX tools optimize efficiency by returning compact observations, executing actions in batches, reporting changes via AX diffs, and guarding against stale states during channel switching.
A supplementary HCU skill guides agents on selecting and coordinating across the three interaction modes effectively.
HCU achieves the highest Partial and Binary task scores on the OSWorld 2.0 benchmark compared to existing systems.
Trajectory analysis demonstrates that evaluated models improve performance, optimize channel allocation differently, and enhance overall operational efficiency.
summary.why_it_matters: Enabling agents to flexibly combine programmatic, semantic, and visual modalities reduces round-trip latency and overcomes the performance bottlenecks of purely visual, human-centric GUI interfaces.

papers.title: On the Opportunities and Challenges of Prefill-to-Autoregressive Cross-Model Transfer

summary.tldr: PLatour is an open-source framework connecting frozen language models via zero-initialized linear bridges for Prefill-to-Autoregressive Cross-model Transfer, paired with PACT-Check to verify genuine communication gains.
key_points: Introduces PLatour, an open-source framework that connects frozen sender and receiver models using lightweight, zero-initialized linear bridges trained via task rewards.
Supports hybrid-attention architectures and outperforms open-source baselines and Mostik on math and coding benchmarks while using a smaller sender model.
Demonstrates that trainable bridges can act merely as parameter-efficient adapters, with performance gains reproducible using uninformative signals, self-communication, or receiver-only training.
Proposes PACT-Check to quantitatively measure the exact portion of performance improvements resulting from actual cross-model communication.
summary.why_it_matters: It provides tools to efficiently combine large and small language models while offering a critical diagnostic method to prevent false attribution of performance gains to latent cross-model communication.

papers.title: Open-HumanScale: An Open Recipe for Scaling Human and Robot Experience for Embodied Foundation Models

summary.tldr: Open-HumanScale provides an open-source recipe and 50,000-hour curated egocentric video corpus (Open-HumanScale-50K) for pretraining embodied world-action models.
key_points: Establishes an empirical log-linear scaling law linking egocentric human pretraining data hours directly to downstream robot task success rates.
Introduces HumanWAM-Vanilla, trained strictly on 50k human video hours, achieving 92.08% Clean2Clean and 68.88% Clean2Random success rates on RoboTwin 2.0.
Develops HumanWAM-Goal using joint human-robot pretraining to reach 84.60% success on RoboTwin 2.0 Clean2Random and unlock zero-shot, parameter-free embodied in-context learning on physical hardware.
Fully open-sources the Open-HumanScale-50K annotated dataset, data curation pipelines, pretraining/post-training code, model checkpoints, and simulation evaluation suites.
summary.why_it_matters: It establishes a reproducible, open-source framework and empirical scaling law for leveraging massive egocentric human video to improve physical robot generalization.

papers.title: The SIMPLE Law for Energy Cost of LLM Inference

summary.tldr: Researchers derived SIMPLE, a four-parameter analytical law that predicts LLM inference energy consumption across model architectures and NVIDIA H100 GPUs without per-LLM calibration.
key_points: Attains R2 = 0.969 and 11.97% MAPE across 13 dense LLMs from six families, reducing error 3.1-3.5x compared to state-of-the-art models.

Derives closed-form computational and memory-access complexities for MHA and GQA, showing prefill energy grows quadratically with hidden dimension and aggressive GQA reduces per-token energy up to 3x versus MHA.
Shows Intelligence per Joule peaks at an intermediate budget and drops up to 3.14x across a 4.0x reasoning token budget range due to super-linear energy growth.

Finds agentic serving increases request energy by 13.0x over non-agentic serving; prefix caching reduces prefill cost by 93% but leaves KV-cache costs unchanged, leaving cached agentic requests 4.8x more expensive.
summary.why_it_matters: It enables accurate, uncalibrated prediction of LLM inference energy costs, uncovering energy inefficiencies in long-context, agentic, and extended reasoning workloads.

papers.title: Towards interpreting any residual stream direction by scaling activation inversion

summary.tldr: Researchers developed Maximally-Activating Example Metamodels (MAEMs) that use a label-free RL objective to generate text exemplars directly from language model residual stream directions, bypassing the limitations of corpus search.
key_points: MAEMs optimize generated text activations to maximize cosine similarity with target residual stream directions using a label-free reinforcement learning objective.
A Qwen3.6-27B MAEM outperformed corpus search (at 10M tokens) and natural-language autoencoders (NLAs) on inverting held-out activations across diverse domains.
The method successfully activated 89% of held-out Sparse Autoencoder (SAE) features, recovered LoRA backdoor payloads better than corpus search, and identified concepts behind steering vectors.
Unlike NLA explanations, MAEM-generated exemplars can be mechanically verified via a standard forward pass on the subject model.
summary.why_it_matters: MAEMs offer a grounded, scalable approach to mechanistically interpret internal model representations without relying on fixed external text corpora or manual labeling.

papers.title: Measured Coupling for Parallel Decoding in Diffusion Language Models

summary.tldr: A new parallel decoding method for diffusion language models uses internal forward-pass probes to directly measure token coupling, improving decoding speed over standard mean-field decoding.
key_points: Replaces similarity-based mean-field proxies with direct measurement of token coupling, defined as how committing one token affects prediction confidence at another.
Calculates coupling metrics using lightweight probes embedded directly inside the main forward pass without requiring extra models or additional training.
Integrates with key-value caching and plugs directly into the existing mean-field decision rule.
Reduces required decoding steps across three models and four benchmarks, achieving faster inference with an average accuracy drop of 1.1 points.
Ablations show that shuffling coupling values or using a uniform bonus eliminates the performance gains.
summary.why_it_matters: It enables faster inference and lower step counts for diffusion language models without requiring model retraining or architectural modifications.

papers.title: First-Token Attraction in Mamba Dynamics

summary.tldr: Researchers established an analytical framework using high-dimensional invariant boxes to prove that the first token acts as an exponential attractor in deep Mamba models, driving token clustering and attention-sink behavior.
key_points: Mamba dynamics feature matrix-valued interaction coefficients lacking positivity guarantees, unlike the positive scalar coefficients in standard attention mechanisms.
The analysis introduces a high-dimensional invariant box paired with a sharp exit-time argument to restore effective sign-definiteness and calculate explicit exponential convergence rates.
The limiting direction of the first token attracts subsequent tokens across deep layers, a dynamic that also generalizes to causal attention, state-space models, and classical time-series models.
Empirical evaluation on Falcon-Mamba-7B confirms that token representation concentration on the first token intensifies with network depth, dominating later layers.
summary.why_it_matters: Proving that Mamba architecture inherently exhibits first-token attraction provides a mathematical foundation for understanding attention-sink phenomena and token clustering in state-space models.

papers.title: SpecCTMC: Exact Speculative Simulation of Diffusion Language Model Continuous-Time Markov Chains

summary.tldr: SpecCTMC is a training-free speculative sampler for masked diffusion language models that reduces sequential evaluations without a separate draft model while preserving the exact continuous-time Markov chain distribution.
key_points: Proposes successive token updates using previously computed model predictions and evaluates intermediate states in parallel.
Applies an exact acceptance-and-correction procedure that maintains the joint distribution of event times, generation order, and token values.
Eliminates both time-discretization errors and additional factorization errors stemming from parallel decoding.
Achieves a 1.73-4.38x reduction in sequential model evaluations on LLaDA-8B-Instruct and Dream-v0-Instruct-7B across five benchmarks.
summary.why_it_matters: It enables significantly faster parallel text generation in diffusion language models while maintaining exact output distribution fidelity without requiring retraining or auxiliary draft models.

papers.title: Beyond K/V Caches: Cross-Model State Handoff in Hybrid Linear-Attention LLMs

summary.tldr: Hybrid State Transfer (HST) enables cross-model state handoff in hybrid linear-attention LLMs by mapping full-attention K/V caches, recurrent states, and convolution histories to bypass prefill during model switches.
key_points: HST handles three state types in hybrid linear-attention models: full-attention (FA) K/V caches, recurrent states (REC), and convolution (Conv) histories.
The method uses structured REC maps, preserves history order during Conv alignment, merges FA cache map updates offline, and calibrates adapters using the frozen target model's continuation outputs.
Model switching evaluations on Qwen3.5 4B to 27B and 9B to 27B achieved 89.88% and 94.11% mean task retention across five benchmarks.
Handoff body speedups of 21.66x (4B to 27B) and 21.91x (9B to 27B) were measured on synthetic 16K inputs when source caches were available.
summary.why_it_matters: HST eliminates the overhead of repeating prefill over long contexts when routing or cascading between different sizes of hybrid linear-attention LLMs.

papers.title: Learning Dynamics of On-Policy Distillation

summary.tldr: A mechanistic framework analyzes how on-policy distillation's feedback loop causes limited student responsiveness and generation degeneration, while showing offline distillation can successfully prepare models for effective on-policy training.
key_points: On-policy distillation (OPD) dynamics are analyzed across two stages: converting distillation signals into parameter updates, and broadcasting updates across prefixes to alter rollout distributions.
Student models can exhibit limited responsiveness despite high teacher-student disagreement due to the underlying update-conversion mechanism.
OPD can cause generation degeneration when local updates aimed at increasing teacher agreement inadvertently raise the probability of unsuccessful continuations, leading to unreliable supervision.

Offline distillation can act as a necessary pre-conditioning phase for OPD, yielding substantial downstream accuracy gains even if immediate held-out accuracy does not improve during the offline phase.
summary.why_it_matters: Understanding OPD's feedback mechanics helps practitioners avoid training degeneration and effectively sequence offline preparation to unlock downstream performance gains in post-training.

papers.title: CoRD: Coupled Rollouts Fill the Blind Spot of On-Policy Distillation

summary.tldr: CoRD improves on-policy distillation by generating rollout states from a geometric interpolation of student and teacher models using maximal coupling from speculative decoding.
key_points: Addresses the blind spot of on-policy distillation by shifting the distribution of training states toward the teacher while retaining the on-policy loss.
Uses maximal coupling to keep student tokens when distributions agree and substitutes teacher tokens from underweighted target distributions only when they disagree.
Evaluated across six base student models (Qwen3 and Qwen3.5, 0.6B to 4B parameters) across five math benchmarks.
Increases average pass@1 by 0.9 to 2.0 points and pass@8 by 1.2 to 3.4 points compared to standard on-policy distillation at equal steps and data.
A 4B student trained with CoRD closes performance gaps on frozen teacher-reached states in 16 steps that standard on-policy distillation fails to reach in 80 steps.
summary.why_it_matters: CoRD provides a more data-efficient sampling mechanism that exposes student models to critical teacher states without needing frequent or ad-hoc state interventions.

papers.title: Masked diffusion as random sequential adsorption: an exactly solvable model for parallel decoding

summary.tldr: Researchers mapped masked diffusion parallel text generation to statistical physics and random sequential adsorption, deriving an exact solution for Markov data and a thermodynamic metric to calculate optimal unmasking schedules.
key_points: Parallel text generation error equals the entropy production of the generation process relative to the reversed masking process.
For Markov data, the generation process is mapped to random sequential adsorption with labelled gaps and solved exactly for any step count.
In the limit of many steps, generation error acts as slowly driven dissipation, where optimal unmasking schedules form geodesics of a closed-form thermodynamic metric derived from mutual information.
Text correlations concentrate error at the start of generation; unmasking schedules that begin with smaller steps reduce path error and perplexity with fewer total steps.
summary.why_it_matters: The theoretical framework enables the mathematical optimization of unmasking schedules to improve speed and output quality in parallel-decoded masked diffusion models.

papers.title: Scaling Laws for SAE Training Data

summary.tldr: Researchers established scaling laws for sparse autoencoder (SAE) training data, demonstrating that replaying a fixed activation buffer after reaching a quality plateau achieves performance equivalent to using entirely fresh activations.
key_points: Identified a trade-off between activation diversity and repetition, showing SAE quality plateaus past a specific buffer size where replaying data yields near-identical results to fresh tokens.
Validated findings across BatchTopK, TopK, and JumpReLU SAE architectures, Llama-3.1 and Qwen3 models, early/middle/late layers, and domain-specific texts like Python code and math.
Evaluated model quality using explained variance (EV), reconstruction MSE, feature absorption, automated interpretability, and sparse probing.
Demonstrated an 8x to 64x reduction in required activation storage with negligible quality loss by replaying the smallest buffer that achieves the quality plateau.
summary.why_it_matters: This approach significantly reduces activation storage requirements by up to 64x during SAE training, dramatically lowering memory bottlenecks and compute costs without sacrificing model interpretability or reconstruction quality.

papers.title: O$^2$PD: Overlap-Gated On-Policy Distillation on Reliable Prefix

summary.tldr: Overlap-gated On-Policy Distillation (O²PD) restricts distillation to the first 20% prefix tokens of student rollouts and uses an overlap-gated α-divergence to address top-k alignment failure modes.
key_points: Applies token-level alignment exclusively to the 20% prefix tokens of student-generated rollouts to ensure teacher supervision remains reliable.
Identifies two key theoretical limitations in standard top-k on-policy distillation: Teacher-support Uncovering and Dominant-Mode Mismatch.
Introduces Reset Support, which pools probability mass outside the teacher top-k into a reset atom, and Support Convergence, which shrinks support to the aligned intersection.
Employs an overlap-gated α-divergence that uses distribution overlap to switch support strategies and dynamically modulate α between mode-covering and mode-seeking objectives.
summary.why_it_matters: O²PD improves student model training efficiency and stability by filtering out unreliable off-policy teacher supervision and resolving support mismatches in top-k distillation.

security.title: Decision Models as Retrieval Gates Against Injection and Pollution

summary.tldr: Open-weight decision models reading raw HTML act as fast retrieval gates to filter indirect prompt injections and web pollution before generation.
key_points: A Kev-4B decision model gate processing passage HTML reduces attack success rates from 27.9% (undefended) and 13.6% (standard mitigations) down to 5.7%.

On a 200-query synthetic web pollution benchmark, filtering candidate pools prior to selecting top-10 passages reduces fake page exposure to 0.5% and maintains 83% accuracy (compared to 28% accuracy without filtering).

The gate requires 76 ms per passage with a low false-positive rate, misclassifying 4 out of 186 benign pages containing human-directed instructions while keeping clean query performance stable (85.6% vs 86.2%).
Filtering input HTML rather than plain text yields higher attack detection rates, and while large LLM judges achieve a higher AUROC (0.99 vs 0.94), the decision gate operates at one-tenth the cost.
summary.why_it_matters: Pre-retrieval filtering using lightweight decision models offers an efficient, low-latency defense against prompt injection and web pollution without relying on expensive LLM generation.

security.title: The Promise of Strategic Agentic Scambaiting

summary.tldr: Researchers present a formal game-theoretic model of agent-to-agent online fraud to evaluate how autonomous defensive scambaiting agents strategically disrupt AI scammers.
key_points: Autonomous scambaiting agents impersonate victims in sustained interactions to extract intelligence like mule bank accounts and crypto wallet addresses for infrastructure takedowns.
The formal mathematical framework models engagement dynamics, resource consumption, belief adaptation, and disruption outcomes between adversarial AI agents.
Scammer operations become unprofitable once defensive baiting-agent prevalence crosses specific operational thresholds.
Under baseline model parameters, defender investment in mimicry quality outpaces equivalent scammer advances in detection capability, favoring defenders as both sides evolve.
summary.why_it_matters: It provides a mathematical foundation showing that scaling autonomous scambaiting agents can systematically undermine the financial viability of AI-driven scam infrastructure.

security.title: Beyond Instruction Override: Benchmarking Indirect Prompt Injection with Task-Tampering Attacks

summary.tldr: A new benchmark evaluates Indirect Prompt Injection (IPI) via task tampering, proving that attacks targeting decision rules, actions, and state achieve higher success rates and evade defenses better than objective-override attacks.
key_points: Defines IPI by source authority rather than instruction-like syntax across 90 validated cases in three tool-use environments.
Categorizes attacks into six decision-making targets: objective, decision rules, available actions, expected consequences, reading of observations, and state beliefs.
Demonstrates that undefended attacks on decision rules, available actions, and state beliefs yield higher mean success rates across five LLMs than traditional objective-targeting attacks.
Shows that a detection-and-removal defense drops objective attack success to 2.4% but leaves observation and state attacks at 9.5% and 12.1% success, respectively.
Reveals that a tool-policy defense only marginally reduces attack success (from 17.0% to 15.4%) because task-tampering attacks retain expected tool calls while manipulating execution values.
summary.why_it_matters: Standard safety evaluations that focus only on task redirection or objective overrides overestimate the coverage of current defenses against indirect prompt injections.

security.title: A Gingerbread House for LLM Agents: Source-Planned Honeypots That Lure Autonomous Attackers into an Isolated Shadow

summary.tldr: A source-planned honeypot defense diverts confirmed autonomous LLM attackers to an isolated shadow application, reducing successful exploits on the real target to zero for the ARTEX attack framework.
key_points: The defense uses an LLM to generate a static honeypot plan from application source code, while a router redirects confirmed attackers' subsequent requests to an isolated shadow instance.
On 40 CVE-Bench tasks, the static plan reduced real target compromise from 26/40 to 5/40 for Claude Opus 4.8, and from 20/40 to 0/40 across 31 valid runs for the ARTEX attack framework.
In a holdout set of 20 new tasks, ARTEX real target compromises dropped from 15/20 to 0/20.
The defense successfully moves working exploits to the shadow in roughly half of deception runs, causing ARTEX to accept planted fake secrets as genuine in 30 out of 120 deception-arm tasks.
Residual security risk relies entirely on unconfirmed attacker requests that reach the real target before routing confirmation occurs.
summary.why_it_matters: It demonstrates that redirecting confirmed autonomous LLM attackers to shadow environments effectively neutralizes fast zero-day exploits without breaking the attacker's execution flow.

security.title: JailBound: FOL-Guided Jailbreak Evaluation for Exploring LLM Behavioral Boundaries

summary.tldr: JailBound introduces an automated jailbreak evaluation framework combining a meta-attack prompt generator with a first-order loss (FOL)-guided dual-branch search to map LLM safety boundaries.
key_points: Uses a fine-tuned meta-attack generator to synthesize evaluation prompts conditioned on risk category, application domain, and attack type.
Employs a first-order loss (FOL)-guided dual-branch search to discover high-value attack states and behavior-sensitive transition states.
Outperforms a zero-order loss (ZOL)-only baseline in High-Value Branch average Attack Success Rate (ASR) by 5.1 and 4.9 percentage points across two test settings.

Demonstrates that states identified by the Safety-Sensitivity Branch exhibit higher behavioral flip rates under local perturbations than High-Value Branch states across all tested radii on JailBound and S-Eval datasets.
Evaluated across 46 LLMs spanning 13 distinct model families under a standardized experimental protocol.
summary.why_it_matters: It enables systematic, automated generation of threat conditions and provides a local sensitivity signal to analyze exact behavioral transitions between safe refusals and jailbreaks.

security.title: Signed but Not Safe: Requirement Integrity in Multi-Agent LLM Handoffs

summary.tldr: A study shows cryptographic HMAC-SHA256 signing of requirement manifests in multi-agent LLM handoffs reduces unsafe commits from 69.4% to 9.0%, establishing requirement extraction as the primary remaining trust boundary.
key_points: HMAC-SHA256 signed manifests reduced unsafe commits under attack from 69.4% to 9.0% using Qwen3-8B across 1,440 trajectories, completely neutralizing in-transit tampering.
Deterministic verifiers out-performed LLM checkers on identical trajectories, achieving a 78.7% detection rate of violating decisions compared to 59.0%, while dropping false alarms from 50% to 7%.

Pre-signing injection attacks exploit the extraction trust boundary, elevating signed-manifest violations from 14.6% to 37.5% in Qwen3-8B, 11.1% to 63.9% in gpt-oss-20b, and 8.3% to 75.0% in GPT-5.6-luna by authenticating corrupted manifests.
summary.why_it_matters: Cryptographically signing extracted requirements prevents middle-agent tampering in LLM workflows, shifting the critical security focus entirely to the initial requirement extraction step.

security.title: Breaking $\mathsf{TraintoDefend}$ via Adaptive Neuron Clustering in Cryptanalytic Model Extraction

summary.tldr: SimBreak is a novel adaptive clustering rule that completely breaks TraintoDefend, raising target layer signature recovery from 0% to 100% on protected fully connected networks.
key_points: TraintoDefend induces neuron weight similarity to group activation state switches, but neurons with similar weights still vary under small perturbations or share only partial normalized weight coordinates.
SimBreak estimates a relative scale across all jointly observed weight coordinates to concurrently evaluate both weight direction and bias consistency.
Evaluated on six protected fully connected networks trained on MNIST, SimBreak achieved 100% target layer signature recovery with a maximum relative recovery error of 2^-22.27.
summary.why_it_matters: It demonstrates that enforcing weight similarity between neurons is insufficient for model confidentiality, invalidating the only known defense against cryptanalytic model extraction.

security.title: Threat actors use agentic AI tooling to find and abuse exposed secrets

summary.tldr: Threat actors are using the ARTEX agentic AI framework to automatically discover exposed secrets in public GitHub repositories and execute follow-on cloud attacks.
key_points: The ARTEX agentic framework rapidly scans public GitHub code for credentials, application IDs, and AI inference API keys without requiring hands-on-keyboard interaction.
In one observed attack, an AI agent escalated from initial GitHub secret scanning to exfiltrating data from Azure Key Vault within five minutes.

Observed malicious activity includes compromised multitenant application credentials used for downstream tenant access, resource discovery, and exfiltration from Azure Storage Accounts and Azure AI services.

Threat infrastructure associated with the campaign includes IP addresses 199.19.77[.]84, 65.87.223[.]26 (exploiting vulnerabilities via user agents), and 157.22.126[.]128 (reconnaissance on Azure AI workloads).
summary.why_it_matters: Agentic AI significantly compresses the attack timeline from secret exposure in public repositories to automated cloud credential exploitation and data exfiltration.

security.title: SPILLWAY: Separating Target Admission from Sanitization to Defend Tool-Using Agents against Prompt Injection

summary.tldr: SPILLWAY separates target admission from sanitization to provide a deterministic, audit-traceable refusal floor that prevents prompt injection attacks against tool-using AI agents without added model-call overhead.
key_points: Target admission deterministically validates action targets using tool output types or pre-set delegation rules without requiring language model checks or prior task planning.
A rule-based sanitizer strips instruction-like regions from tool returns before model consumption, logging removed spans as auditable evidence.
A local judge can override false-positive refusals, but it is explicitly blocked from restoring calls targeting text removed by the sanitizer.

SPILLWAY achieved a 0.0 attack success rate against standard templated injections and forged chat templates across three model backbones, and a 0.007 mean attack success rate under a reinforcement-learning attacker.
summary.why_it_matters: It allows autonomous agents handling sensitive email, file, and payment operations to block prompt injection attacks deterministically without requiring extra model calls or sacrificing utility.

security.title: CANMentor: A Large-Small Model Collaboration Framework for CAN Bus Intrusion Detection

summary.tldr: CANMentor pairs a vehicle-side lightweight IDS with a cloud-side LLM teacher, using privacy-preserving proxies and latency-aware prediction switching to continuously improve local detection via soft target knowledge distillation.
key_points: A privacy-aware generator converts original vehicle CAN messages into proxies before uploading them to the cloud-side LLM teacher to mitigate data exposure.
Vehicles execute local inference immediately and only accept cloud predictions if received within a defined latency bound, retaining local predictions otherwise.
Returned teacher logits act as soft targets for periodic local knowledge distillation to address performance degradation caused by non-IID data.

Evaluations on non-IID partitions of the ROAD and HCRL datasets achieved maximum relative Macro F1 improvements of 25.01% and 20.79% via distillation, and improved accuracy near local decision boundaries by 38.71–42.00 percentage points.
summary.why_it_matters: It enables lightweight, resource-constrained vehicle intrusion detection systems to achieve high generalization on non-IID data without compromising raw CAN payload privacy or real-time latency requirements.

security.title: MEvince: Knowledge-Constrained LLM Reasoning for Technique Identification from Malware Reports

summary.tldr: MEvince is a knowledge-constrained LLM framework that maps malware reports to MITRE ATT&CK techniques using shared behavioral representations, primitive-guided extraction, and evidence-aligned retrieval.
key_points: Uses a shared behavioral representation built via agentic mining of technique documentation to link report observations directly to technique definitions.
Employs primitive-guided extraction to structure observations and evidence-aligned retrieval to compare candidate techniques alongside confusable alternatives.
Incorporates validation controls to verify evidence references and enforce technique-specific behavioral requirements without updating model parameters.
Outperformed 11 baselines on a dataset of 610 public MITRE ATT&CK malware reports, boosting exact-ID F1 by 17.4% over the strongest baseline.
Increased gold-label candidate retrieval coverage from 31.6% to 47.9%, with offline agentic audits enabling parameter-free adaptation.
summary.why_it_matters: It significantly improves automated, reliable mapping of complex malware reports to ATT&CK techniques without requiring expensive model fine-tuning.

security.title: New investments to reduce on-premises security risk

summary.tldr: Microsoft announced an on-premises security initiative featuring On-Premises Baseline Security Mode to harden supported Exchange, SharePoint, and Skype for Business servers by default.
key_points: Introduces On-Premises Baseline Security Mode to automatically maintain secure configurations and reduce manual administrator setup across three areas: Patch, Configure, and Protect.
Targeting automatic application of security updates in Q1 CY2027 after a fixed period post-release for connected SharePoint Server, Exchange Server, and Skype for Business Server environments.
Since September 2026, Microsoft releases Important security updates outside of the traditional Patch Tuesday schedule alongside Critical updates when faster action is required.
Integrates guidance through Secure Now, offering risk prioritization alongside an AI readiness checklist in Microsoft Security Exposure Management.
summary.why_it_matters: The initiative automates patch deployment and default configuration baselines for critical on-premises servers, shortening the window of vulnerability against fast-moving AI-driven attack tools.

summary.tldr: Microsoft's November 2026 security updates introduce agentic AI controls alongside enhancements to Intune Endpoint Privilege Management and Microsoft Defender Experts.
key_points: Dynamic Permissions and Dynamic Agent Risk scope AI agent authority to specific tasks, using Dynamic Conditional Access to narrow permissions or require human approval if risk changes.

Microsoft Execution Containers (MXC) achieved general availability, delivering an OS-enforced containment layer on Windows to apply least-privilege boundaries across files, networks, processes, and user interactions.

Microsoft Intune Endpoint Privilege Management added system settings support, enabling standard users to alter IPv4, IPv6, and DNS server values with optional business justification or Windows authentication requirements.
Microsoft Defender portal consolidated its Defender Experts MDR experiences into a central overview page featuring updated navigation and visibility into active and completed threat hunts.
summary.why_it_matters: These features provide administrators with granular, dynamic access boundaries for both human users and AI agents to enforce least-privilege security at scale.

security.title: AI Governance Isn't a Chore Problem. It's an Architecture Problem.

summary.tldr: Senior business leaders are experiencing a 26% increase in working hours due to manual AI risk management, revealing that governance is being handled through reactive triage rather than embedded architecture.
key_points: According to a September 2026 OneTrust survey, 80% of senior decision-makers spend more time managing AI risk.
Average working hours for these leaders have increased by 26% due to governance workloads.
Current operational failures stem from treating governance as a manual process of chasing unapproved tools, triaging incidents, and reconstructing decisions rather than an architectural design.
summary.why_it_matters: Attempting to manage AI risk through manual processes and administrative oversight burdens leadership without solving fundamental operational security issues.

summary.tldr: LABBA integrates a lightweight LLM-based contextual reasoning module with a novel phone-blowing acoustic behavioral biometric technique to enhance continuous authentication robustness.
key_points: Uses blow-acoustic signals collected from users, extracting temporal and spectral features to build similarity representations.
Converts extracted features into structured prompts using either discrete rule-based categories or continuous normalized scores.
Evaluated on a dataset of 50 participants under diverse behavioral, contextual, and environmental conditions.
Achieved 99.46% accuracy in rule-based mode and 99.38% accuracy in score-based mode, outperforming traditional non-LLM baselines.
summary.why_it_matters: Incorporating LLMs into behavioral biometrics improves adaptability to real-world user variability and context changes over static threshold systems.

infra.title: Configure, Certify, and Operate Kubernetes GPU Clusters with NVIDIA DSX OS

summary.tldr: NVIDIA DSX OS helps operators configure, certify, and manage Kubernetes GPU clusters to detect silent performance degradation.
key_points: Underperforming GPUs can degrade entire distributed training jobs despite passing basic system health checks.
System performance shifts across a cluster's lifecycle due to node replacements, driver updates, and ongoing hardware changes.
NVIDIA DSX OS targets cluster operational management across configuration, certification, and execution stages.
summary.why_it_matters: Detecting degraded GPUs before workload execution prevents wasted compute resources and slowdowns in large-scale distributed AI workloads.

infra.title: Five Ways NVIDIA Co-Design Maximizes the Value of Every Byte in the AI Factory

summary.tldr: NVIDIA leverages full-stack hardware and software co-design to maximize token output per byte by optimizing High Bandwidth Memory (HBM) utilization in AI factories.
key_points: High Bandwidth Memory (HBM) operates as the fastest, most expensive, and most constrained memory tier in AI factory infrastructure.
System optimization focuses on maximizing useful work per byte rather than simply increasing raw GPU memory capacity.
Eliminating redundant weight copies, idle session KV caches, and recomputed prefixes directly frees HBM capacity for active token generation.
summary.why_it_matters: Optimizing HBM efficiency through full-stack co-design directly increases token throughput and reduces operational waste in large-scale AI workloads.

infra.title: More Performance From Every Byte: How Full-Stack Codesign Solves AI’s Memory Challenge

summary.tldr: NVIDIA is using full-stack codesign across hardware, software, and memory hierarchies to increase GPU memory efficiency and overcome HBM capacity and bandwidth limits for large AI models.
key_points: Agentic applications and RAG inflate memory pressure by processing contexts up to 3 million tokens, causing KV cache and trillion-parameter model weights to compete for limited GPU HBM.
Relying solely on adding HBM capacity hits a memory wall where fixed memory bandwidth cannot supply data fast enough to match GPU compute capacity, increasing costs and power consumption.
NVIDIA manages data across a multi-tiered hierarchy spanning GPU HBM, CPU memory, local SSDs, and shared storage to place data on the optimal tier based on speed and cost.
Full-stack optimizations like the NVFP4 precision format reduce model weight storage requirements compared to Hopper's FP8 format.
Despite HBM capacity per GPU increasing by only ~3% from Blackwell Ultra to Vera Rubin, agentic throughput per dollar increased up to 30x on the SemiAnalysis AgentX benchmark.
summary.why_it_matters: Full-stack memory management enables AI factories to scale agentic inference throughput and context lengths affordably without being constrained by HBM supply shortages and cost limits.

infra.title: Vera Delivers the Best of Both Worlds: Highest Throughput and Fastest Agents

summary.tldr: NVIDIA announced performance metrics for its Vera CPU, demonstrating higher agent execution speed and greater power efficiency compared to leading x86 processors across various partner workloads.
key_points: In a 100MW data center comparison, Vera delivered 1.6x more agents per watt versus the fastest x86 CPU and 2x faster agent speed compared to the most energy-efficient x86 CPU.
Daytona initialized 1,000 agent sandboxes in 10.8 seconds on Vera versus 88.4 seconds on x86, achieving 12.7 completed jobs per second across 2,000 concurrent sandboxes.
ClickHouse scaled near-linearly across 176 cores without specific tuning, while DuckLabs reached ~1.5x the median TPC-H SF1000 performance of an Intel Xeon 6 baseline.
Early production testing showed agentic speedups of 1.5x at Perplexity and up to 2.2x at DeepInfra compared to traditional x86 processors.
summary.why_it_matters: AI infrastructure operators can deploy a single CPU architecture to maximize both agent execution speed and task capacity within strict power-density constraints.

infra.title: Use NVIDIA NeMo to Turn Agent Failures into Tests and Harness Fixes

summary.tldr: NVIDIA NeMo enables developers to convert production agent failures into prioritized issues and domain-specific evaluations to improve agent performance.
key_points: Captures production evidence to address domain-specific failures that generic benchmarks miss.
Systematically improves agent components including prompts, tools, models, memory, skills, and harness code.
Targets operational issues such as incorrect tool selection, flawed workflow branching, missing context, and inefficient model usage.
summary.why_it_matters: It allows developers to continuously refine domain-specific AI agents using real-world failure data rather than relying on unrepresentative standard benchmarks.

infra.title: Build a semantic layer for agentic AI with EDB Postgres AI and Amazon Bedrock AgentCore

summary.tldr: EDB Postgres AI introduces a database-native semantic layer (SemKB) via its AIDB extension, exposing schema metadata, foreign keys, and access controls directly to external agentic AI using Amazon Bedrock AgentCore and MCP endpoints.
key_points: AIDB uses standard Postgres COMMENT ON statements and aidb.create_semantic_alias to define business logic, while relying on foreign keys to automatically build join paths across schema tables.
The operational Postgres database hosts an internal Model Context Protocol (MCP) endpoint, which is exposed to agents via an Application Load Balancer and registered on AgentCore Gateway.

Data governance and privacy rely natively on Postgres GRANT statements, column-level security, and row-level security (RLS), allowing different authorization roles to produce distinct query results using identical prompt and tool setups.
AIDB provides direct observability by logging OpenTelemetry traces for every database-executed SQL statement as queryable rows inside the aidb_otel schema.
summary.why_it_matters: Embedding the semantic layer and security governance directly inside the operational database eliminates the need for separate advisory prompt controls or external virtualization layers when serving agentic AI workflows.

infra.title: Prepare web content for Amazon Bedrock Knowledge Bases with Crawl4AI

summary.tldr: AWS details a custom web ingestion pipeline for Amazon Bedrock Knowledge Bases using Crawl4AI to output structured Markdown and metadata sidecars to Amazon S3.
key_points: Uses Crawl4AI's DefaultMarkdownGenerator with a pruning content filter to eliminate boilerplate like navigation while keeping tables, lists, and headings.
Targeted extraction limits parsing to specific CSS selectors, origin seeds, depth caps, page limits, and URL pattern constraints.
Generates custom metadata sidecar files alongside Markdown in Amazon S3 to enable metadata filtering during Amazon Bedrock Knowledge Base retrieval.
Runs as a batch ingestion pipeline via AWS Fargate tasks triggered by Amazon EventBridge before handoff to Bedrock for parsing, chunking, and embedding.
summary.why_it_matters: It allows developers to clean web data and inject custom metadata prior to ingestion, improving retrieval quality for complex websites that the native Amazon Bedrock Web Crawler cannot process cleanly.

vendors.title: GPT‑6 Cyber: Advancing the frontier of aligned cybersecurity agents

Capable of developing code fixes for detected vulnerabilities.
Trained with alignment constraints to operate strictly within authorized boundaries.
summary.why_it_matters: It provides a targeted AI agent that automates both vulnerability discovery and remediation while enforcing scope boundaries.

Designed to enable interactive and dynamic environment generation.
summary.why_it_matters: Open interactive world models provide developers with accessible tools to simulate physical environments for robotics and AI development.

summary.tldr: Anthropic has detailed its Long-Term Benefit Trust (LTBT), an independent governance body designed to select and ultimately control a majority of the company's Board of Directors.
key_points: The LTBT consists of an independent body of five financially disinterested trustees.
Trustees have the authority to elect and remove Anthropic Board members, with their representation growing over time to a majority.
The structure pairs with Anthropic's Public Benefit Corporation status to address non-market externalities and align governance with public interest over purely stockholder financial interests.
summary.why_it_matters: By granting board election and removal power to a non-financially interested trust, Anthropic shifts core corporate accountability away from exclusive stockholder control toward broader societal impacts.
